name: Charisma AI
tagline: Platform for building conversational characters that mix scripted and generated dialogue.
best_for: Training simulations, branded campaigns and interactive stories
description:
Charisma AI is a platform for building virtual characters you can talk to. Instead of a single chatbot, you design characters inside a visual graph or script editor, mixing lines you wrote yourself with generated responses. Characters can remember earlier turns and adapt as a conversation goes on, and projects can hold several characters and long branching dialogues.

It is aimed at teams making training simulations, brand campaigns and interactive stories, along with creators and enterprises that need governance. Experiences can be deployed to web, mobile, VR and game engines through SDKs. Check the official site for current plans and credit rules.
use_steps: Create an account and open a new story project.
Add a character and sketch the conversation in the visual graph editor.
Write scripted lines and set where generated replies are allowed.
Test the dialogue in the preview, then deploy through an SDK or embed.
pros: No-code visual editors for dialogue flow
Mix of scripted and generative lines
Guardrails and role-based permissions suit teams
Deploys to web, mobile, VR and game engines
cons: Learning the graph model takes time
Credit-based billing needs watching on long projects
features: Visual graph and script flow editors
pricing_details: Described as freemium with pay-as-you-go credits and enterprise options. Plans change, so check the official site.

faq.q: What is Charisma AI used for?
faq.a: It is used to build conversational characters for training, marketing and interactive storytelling, combining written dialogue with generated replies.

faq.q: Do I need to code to use it?
faq.a: The editors are visual and no-code, though deploying into a game engine or app uses the provided SDKs.
It is described as pay-as-you-go with credits and enterprise tiers for heavier use; confirm current terms on the official site.

name: BeyondWords

description:

It is built for publishers, content marketers and media brands, especially those producing many articles. It includes a voice editor, scheduling, analytics on listens and completion, an API for bulk automation and CMS integrations such as WordPress. Check the official site for current plans and voice options.

name: Decopy AI
tagline: Browser toolkit for AI text detection, rewriting AI drafts and summarizing.
best_for: Marketers, students and editors checking or polishing AI-assisted text
description:
Decopy AI bundles several text utilities in a browser. It can estimate whether text or an image was produced by AI, rewrite AI-sounding drafts into more natural wording, and summarize articles and YouTube videos. Extras such as OCR and multi-language support are part of the same library.

It is aimed at marketers, students, educators and SEO teams who publish AI-assisted content and want a quick review step. Detection tools give estimates, not proof, so treat the result as a prompt for human editing. A browser extension is also mentioned. Check the official site for current limits and privacy terms.

Paste your text or upload the image or video link.
Run the tool and read the result or rewritten draft.
Edit the output by hand and keep your own voice.

name: Hume AI
tagline: Expressive voice platform with emotion-aware text-to-speech and real-time voice interface.
best_for: Developers and creators building expressive voice apps
description:
Hume AI builds voice tools that pay attention to emotion. Octave is its text-to-speech engine, which predicts expression, cadence and prosody from the text. EVI is a real-time speech-to-speech interface that picks up emotional cues in a speaker's voice and responds accordingly, and a separate API measures emotional expression in audio, video, images and text.

Developers, customer-service teams and content creators are the main audience, and the product also targets regulated fields such as healthcare and finance. Voices can be designed from a text description or cloned from a sample, and you can connect your own language model. Expressiveness is strongest in English. Check the official site for current plans.

Describe or clone a voice, or choose one from the library.
Generate speech from text, or connect EVI to your app with an SDK.
Test with different emotional prompts and adjust the voice.
pros: Voice design from a text description
cons: Developer setup is needed for the real-time interface
pricing_details: A free tier and usage-based paid plans are described, with enterprise pricing. Plans change; check the official site.

faq.a: EVI is Hume's real-time speech-to-speech interface that detects emotional cues in a voice and replies with a matching tone.

name: Resound
tagline: Browser-based AI podcast editor that cuts filler words and silences.
best_for: Podcasters who want faster first-pass editing
description:
Resound is a podcast editor that runs in the browser. It detects filler sounds such as ums and ahs and long silences, then marks them in a visual waveform so you can accept or reject each suggested cut. It can also reduce background noise, level volume, mix multiple tracks and master to loudness standards.

Hobbyists and professional podcast networks are the target, and no audio-editing background is assumed. Files export as MP3 or WAV. According to its FAQ there are no direct DAW timeline exports or API integrations, so it works best as a quick cleanup step. Check the official site for current plan limits.
use_steps: Upload your recording to a new project.
Run filler-word and silence detection.
Review suggested edits on the waveform and accept or reject them.
Enhance, mix and master, then export MP3 or WAV.
pros: Review each suggested cut before applying
pricing_details: A free plan with limited monthly editing exists; paid tiers add time and features. Check the official site.

faq.a: It suggests edits that you accept or reject in the waveform.
MP3 and WAV.

faq.q: Can I send the project to my DAW?
faq.a: Its FAQ says there are no direct DAW timeline exports.

name: SquadCast
tagline: Remote recording studio that captures each guest locally and uploads to the cloud.
best_for: Podcasters and video producers recording remote interviews
description:
SquadCast is a cloud-based studio for recording remote conversations. Each participant's audio and video is recorded on their own device and uploaded progressively, so a shaky connection during the call does not damage the final files. Every guest gets a separate track, with lossless WAV audio and up to 4K video listed.

Guests join through a link in the browser with nothing to download, which keeps things simple for non-technical interviewees. The page names Chrome and says there are no native apps. It connects to Descript for editing and transcription and offers Dropbox integration and API access. SquadCast is owned by Descript. A short free trial is offered; check the official site for current plans.
use_steps: Create a session and invite guests with a link.
Have guests join in Chrome and test their mic and camera.
Record and let local files upload to the cloud.
Download separate tracks or send them to Descript.
pros: Local recording protects against connection drops
features: Lossless WAV and up to 4K video
pricing_details: No permanent free plan; a 7-day free trial is described. Check the official site for current plans.

faq.a: Local capture means call quality issues do not affect the saved files.
No, they join from a browser through a link.
The listing states that Descript owns it.

name: Weavy (Figma Weave)
tagline: Node-based canvas that chains AI models and editing tools into reusable pipelines.
best_for: Creative teams needing repeatable multi-model image and video workflows
description:
Weavy, now Figma Weave, is a browser canvas where you connect steps as nodes: generate an image with one model, refine it, composite it, then send it to video. Pipelines can be saved and shared, so a look that took effort to build can be repeated by others.

It lists models from many providers and editing tools such as masking, relighting, outpainting, upscaling and inpainting. App Mode builds a simplified interface from a workflow for people who do not want to touch nodes. Founded in 2024, it was acquired by Figma in late 2025, and the two products currently have separate billing and credits. Check the official site for current plans.
use_steps: Open a new workflow on the canvas.
Add a model node and a prompt, and generate a first image.
Chain editing nodes such as upscaling or compositing.
Save the workflow and share it, optionally through App Mode.
cons: Node graphs have a learning curve
pricing_details: A free tier with monthly credits and paid per-user plans are described. Plans change; check the official site.

faq.a: Yes, the product is now called Figma Weave and runs separately from Figma.

name: Enhancor
tagline: Restores skin texture on AI-generated portraits that look plastic.

description:

It is built for creators and small studios, mostly for tight head-and-shoulder shots. Batch processing, job queues and side-by-side previews with sliders speed up larger sets. Output is HD on entry plans and up to 4K on higher tiers, with exports meant to move into tools like Photoshop, Lightroom or Canva. Export and finish in your usual editor.
